profiles.identity_context: A. A. Toivonen was the business manager of Industrialisti, the Finnish-language newspaper supporting the Industrial Workers of the World in Duluth, Minnesota. profiles.name: Topias Kekkonen
profiles.query: "Topias Kekkonen" Industrialisti IWW Duluth 1920 portrait photograph archive
profiles.identity_context: Topias Kekkonen, also recorded as Tobias Kekkonen, edited Industrialisti, a Finnish-language newspaper supporting the Industrial Workers of the World in Duluth, Minnesota. The One Big Union Monthly reported his arrest on January 20, 1920, and prosecution under Minnesota's criminal-syndicalism law over the newspaper's political writing. By June 1920 he was out on bail after a guilty verdict. On December 2, 1921, the Minnesota Supreme Court upheld his conviction in State v. Workers' Socialist Publishing Co., 150 Minn. 406. A February 6, 1922, Oregonian report describes a sentence imposed February 4 of a $1,000 fine or one year's imprisonment. That alternative penalty does not establish that he served a year in prison.
profiles.finding: Contemporary One Big Union Monthly and University of Oregon Toveri1920 reporting corroborate editor's arrest. Finnish-language follow-up returned modern namesakes; no verified portrait located.
